diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17. The live OLT sees one responding ONU at that slot, so one of the CRM records is stale or incorrectly mapped, creating an inventory and provisioning conflict.
evidence: The target ONU is online, responds to SNMP, completes authentication, and has normal optical readings: RX about -20.9 dBm and TX about +2.4 dBm.
Seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable, distance remains constant at 134, and TX bias current remains within the healthy range, ruling out fibre, laser, and distance faults.
The OLT, router, PON port, VLAN 1044, RADIUS entry, and subscriber sessions are all operational and within normal limits.
The port has a direct duplicate-slot conflict: two different active line IDs are assigned to EPON0/4:17, although only one ONU can occupy that physical slot.
The live PON probe confirms a single online ONU at index 17, supporting a CRM/inventory duplication rather than a PON or OLT hardware failure.
The issue is therefore localized to the EPON0/4 slot assignment and requires record reconciliation.

remediation.action: Query the OLT for the actual ONU MAC and match it to the two CRM records. Retain the correct customer-to-slot assignment, remove or deactivate the stale duplicate record, and correct any associated inventory/provisioning data. Do not alter the active ONU service until the MAC ownership is confirmed. Re-run the slot and authentication checks afterward.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
